title: Tiered entitlement fallback and automated credit reconciliation PRD
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem statement: As customers adopt flexible plans and multi-route architectures, our current single-dimension quota model leads to abrupt service denials, manual billing adjustments, and high-support overhead. We need a deterministic entitlement system that permits graceful fallback between quota dimensions (route-level, model-level, pooled credits), supports soft-cap behavior with automated retries, and performs automated credit reconciliation/refunds for shortfalls. This PRD defines requirements, acceptance criteria, scope, and rollout plan for implementing: 1) multi-dimensional entitlements and priority fallback policies, 2) soft-cap windows with adaptive throttling and retry hints, and 3) automated credit reconciliation and pro-rated refunds for transient shortfalls.
background: Current issues observed from billing tickets: - Customers with both per-route and pooled plan credits frequently hit hard caps on one route while other credits remain unused, causing outages and support tickets. - Manual invoice adjustments for transient overages (~<24h spikes) are common and costly. - Engineering has partial safety nets (rate-limit 429s, global overage toggles) but no deterministic policy for fallback to pooled credits or lower-fidelity model variants. - Product needs to reduce support load, improve developer UX, and provide predictable economics for customers.
goals: 1) Reduce customer-impacting hard-quotas by enabling safe, auditable fallbacks to secondary entitlements. 2) Reduce manual invoice adjustments by 60% for transient shortfalls via automated reconciliation and pro-rated refunds. 3) Provide clear billing semantics and acceptance criteria so SRE and Billing can automate enforcement and ledger updates. 4) Ensure rollout can be toggled per-customer and observed in Console with clear indicators.
non_goals: 1) Full redesign of pricing plans or introduction of new paid tiers. 2) Replacing existing metering infra; we will extend the current metering events. 3) Complex cross-tenant credit sharing (out of scope for this iteration).
requirements: Functional requirements: - Entitlement graph: model entities for route, model-variant, customer pooled bucket, and global backup credits. - Fallback policies: allow configuring ordered fallback chains (e.g., route -> pooled -> model-variant-low-cost -> emergency-burst) with per-step limits and priority weights. - Soft-cap behavior: when a quota threshold (configurable %, default 95%) is crossed, begin returning 'soft-throttle' responses with Retry-After hints and metrics; allow short-lived overage window (default 10 minutes) before hard-deny. - Automated reconciliation: detect shortfall events where over-usage is within reconciliation window (default 24h) and automatically debit pooled credits or issue pro-rated refunds without manual intervention, based on rules. - Billing ledger integration: produce immutable ledger entries for every fallback and reconciliation action with metadata linking to requests, routes, and customer entitlements. - Audit & explainability: Console shows a timeline of entitlement decisions per customer with links to invoices and metering events. - Config APIs: allow Enterprise admins to opt in/opt out per-customer and set fallback chains and soft-cap windows. Non-functional requirements: - Latency: decision path must add <5ms p95 to request path for hosted API. - Reliability: fallback decision service must be HA with 99.99% uptime and observable metrics. - Security: all entitlement actions must be recorded for audit; access control per account.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Fallback chains can be configured via the admin API and saved to customer configuration; unit and integration tests demonstrate ordered evaluation.

AC-2: In a staged test, when route quota is exceeded but pooled credits exist, traffic automatically drains from route quota and consumes pooled credits without 403s; metrics reflect the switch and ledger entries are generated.

AC-3: Soft-cap behavior: when usage reaches configured threshold, we return a new soft-throttle response (HTTP 429 with X-Soft-Throttle header and Retry-After) for non-critical requests; critical priority requests are allowed into the overage window up to configured limit.

AC-4: Automated reconciliation: for overage events shorter than reconciliation window, system automatically applies pooled credits or issues a pro-rated invoice refund; finance tests reconcile ledgers and observe no manual adjustment required for 95% of test cases.
AC-5: Billing audit: every fallback and reconciliation action has an immutable ledger entry with request IDs, timestamps, and entitlement path; entries are visible in Console and exportable via CSV.
AC-6: Performance: entitlement decision path latency added by new service is <5ms p95 in production traffic simulation; no measurable increase in token-serving latency beyond noise.
AC-7: Rollout controls: feature flags exist to enable per-customer and per-route toggles; canary rollout shows metrics for impact prior to 100% enablement.
AC-8: Security: audit logs preserved for 180 days by default and accessible to support with RBAC; security review signoff completed prior to GA.
AC-9: Documentation: Customer-facing docs and Console help text updated and linked; SDKs updated with examples for fallback-aware error handling.
success_metrics: Reduce manual billing adjustments for transient overages by >=60% within 3 months of GA.
Decrease customer-initiated hard quota-related incidents by 50% in Q2 after rollout.
Ensure 99% of reconciliation events are automated and require no human intervention.
P95 entitlement decision latency <5ms and no regression to token latency SLA.
detailed_design_notes: - Entitlement graph will be implemented as a small, strongly-consistent service backed by existing metering DB. - Decision path evaluation is a prioritized linear scan with short-circuiting; caching of resolved policy per-customer to meet latency SLO. - Ledger writes are appended to the billing write-ahead queue (extend existing stream) and reconciled by a scheduled job. - For emergency fallback to lower-fidelity model, integrate with routing policy to select model-variant tagged 'fallback-low-cost'. - Console UX: new 'Entitlement timeline' panel on Billing tab and per-route usage page with TTL filtered view. - Edge cases: partial request consumption (streaming generation mid-response) will be charged to the entitlement active when the token was emitted; system will attribute tokens by token-range to entitlements for accurate reconciliation.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (4 weeks): design entitlement schema, APIs, and admin controls; implement decision service prototype and unit tests. Phase 2 (6 weeks): integrate with metering pipeline, ledger write path, and reconciliation job; add soft-cap behaviors and headers for SDKs. Phase 3 (3 weeks): Console UI, docs, and SDK updates; internal canary on 5 pilot customers + observe for 2 weeks. Phase 4 (2 weeks): wider rollout with feature flags and post-launch monitoring. Total estimated sprint weeks: 15.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal alpha: enable for billing team and 2 internal customers. 2) Pilot: 5 enterprise customers opt-in; monitor reconciliation accuracy and support tickets. 3) Progressive rollout: 25% of customers, then 50%, 100% with 48h observation windows. 4) Post-GA: evaluate metrics and consider default enablement for new customers.
monitoring_and_observability: Dashboards: entitlement decisions per minute, fallback rates by route, reconciliation success rate, reconciliation latency, refunds issued, ledger write failures. Alerts: reconciliation job failure >3% over 1h, fallback rate spike >baseline +30% for 1h, ledger write queue lag >30s.
security_and_compliance: All entitlement decisions and ledger entries are immutable and signed; data retention aligns with billing retention policy. Customers in regulated regions can opt for on-prem ledger replication. Security Review checklist: encryption at rest and in transit for entitlement service, RBAC for admin APIs, auditability of reconciliation actions.
out_of_scope_details: - Dynamic per-token pricing changes. - Cross-tenant credit pooling beyond explicitly configured enterprise tenants. - Complex legal refund workflows (will trigger finance approval for unusual cases).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental unbounded fallback could exhaust pooled credits. Mitigation: per-customer global safety cap and automated alerting on pooled burn rate. Risk: reconciliation mis-attribution for streaming requests. Mitigation: token attribution unit tests and end-to-end simulation harness. Risk: customer confusion over fallback semantics. Mitigation: clear Console explanations, API response headers, and SDK helpers.
open_questions: 1) Default soft-cap threshold: 95% vs 90%? Recommend 95% to reduce noise. 2) Should we allow negative pooled balances for emergency burst? Recommend no; instead allow configured emergency-burst credit with explicit approval. 3) Reconciliation window default: 24h vs 72h? Recommend 24h to reduce finance latency.
notes: Coordinate with Finance (billing reconciliation team) and SRE early. Schedule a brown-bag to align on ledger schema and export formats. Ensure SDK teams are looped in for header semantics and sample code.
qa_plan: Create end-to-end test harness that simulates multi-route traffic patterns, injection of high-frequency spikes, and streaming token attribution. Run reconciliation runs against a shadow ledger and compare outputs. Test canary customers in staging with synthetic traffic before enabling in prod.
billing_acceptance_criteria: All reconciliation adjustments appear on draft invoices within configured window and are reflected in final invoices with correct pro-rated amounts.
Finance team confirms ledger integrity via automated reconciliation checks (no unmatched entries >0.1% in sample runs).
Refunds or credit grants are automatically posted and visible in customer billing history with link to underlying entitlement event.
Billing exports include entitlement metadata (route, fallback path, reconciliation_reason) for downstream accounting systems.
